evidence.reason: The default allowlist is ordered as the 18 legacy names followed by ONCHAIN_FEATURE_NAMES, and candidate_rule_feature_columns returns that list in supplied_ff mode at features/catalog.py:28-36. However, the production catalog then unconditionally applies _remove_low_dispersion at features/catalog.py:80-85, and the pipeline uses build_rule_feature_specs at run_pipeline.py:3438-3440. A required feature that is constant or more than 95% NaN can therefore make the actual Phase 2 catalog contain 29 or fewer features. The added exact-count tests exercise candidates with varying values at tests/unit/test_onchain_feature_contract.py:32-42, not this production failure mode.

The supplied_ff branch correctly rejects missing allowlisted columns and excludes generated LWC/MTF columns, while the generated_lwc branch remains separate at lines 38-56. The exact-30 candidate sub-contract passes, but the full production-catalog criterion is not guaranteed after dispersion filtering.

The MTF merge keeps only columns in the OHLCV/base-label/internal set or the allowlisted RULE_ALLOWED_FF_FEATURES at lines 236-245. Its right side admits only MTF score columns and lwc_* columns at lines 246-251, so arbitrary ff_*, hwc_*, and mwc_* inputs cannot survive.

The integration test supplies an allowed legacy and on-chain feature plus ff_legacy_lwc and hwc_stale_feature, then asserts allowed features survive and arbitrary ff_/HWC/MWC artifacts do not at lines 498-507.

A bounded_continuous scale-1.0 entry is inferred for an on-chain column from training values at lines 183-189, but apply_fuzzy_feature_scaling divides and clips every manifest entry at lines 217-229, including bounded_continuous values.

The normal split path applies the train-fitted scaling to train, validation, validation-fitness, and validation-selection frames at lines 3210-3212. The only runtime range check is later in _run_phase2 at lines 3472-3474. A valid training frame with a validation value of 2.5 is clipped to 1.0 before the check, so Phase 2 does not reject the out-of-range input and the supplied value is silently changed. An all-infinite training column also satisfies finite.size == 0 at fuzzy_scaling.py:184 and is clipped instead of rejected.

The added test sends a bad frame directly to _run_phase2 at lines 720-725. It does not exercise _load_and_split_data's scaling-before-validation order, so it cannot detect the validation-value clipping failure.
The RSI computation and midline transform remain unchanged at lines 251-253; only the duplicate rsi_14 assignment is absent.
The test still checks the generated feature output and explicitly requires rsi_14_midline, rejects rsi_14, and checks the warm-up NaN at lines 141-159.

feature_contract_digest does hash the ordered allowlist, source mode, registry version, selected transform fields, and the top-level manifest contract_digest at lines 100-119. It is recorded in dataset and ledger records at lines 129-138 and 180-185, and in the Phase 2 resume identity at run_pipeline.py:531-540.

Split-cache loading checks split geometry, source_sha256, artifact hashes, and frame structure at lines 384-419, but never compares a feature_contract_digest. run_pipeline.py:3122-3131 only checks that cached train data has the 30 column names. Changing the mode or on-chain manifest digest while keeping the same 30 columns and CSV/artifact bytes therefore reuses the stale split.

MTF composition loads existing HWC, MWC, and LWC archives at lines 4407-4441 without comparing their lineage to the current feature_contract_digest. The MTF manifest merely records the current digest at lines 4013-4015, which can relabel an old archive instead of rejecting it. The archive loader validates schema and stored hashes only at mtf/archives.py:381-382.

Standalone strategy loading accepts a valid on-disk RB output through Output_Writer at lines 795-807. MTF checks at lines 814-869 bind archive hashes to the stored strategy manifest, not to the current feature contract, and non-MTF strategies have no current digest comparison. Thus stale RB outputs can still be evaluated after a contract change.

The persistent Phase 2 archive validator compares only the feature_signature at lines 2792-2799; save_archive emits that signature without a feature-contract digest at lines 4156-4160. The sidecar Phase 2 resume identity is covered, but the persistent archive path is not.
validate_config checks exactly 30 unique ff_* names and the source mode at lines 2708-2713; the deterministic verification command in the review package reports printed output 30.

Under the supplied_ff production branch, HWC/MWC context scores are added only as MTF runtime columns and are not in the 30-feature allowlist. The MTF merge keeps them separate from supplied features.
Scaling is fitted from train_df and then applied to validation/test-style frames; the changed code does not use test or forward data to define feature names, transforms, or winners.

The tracked BASE..HEAD package lists exactly the 15 requested changed files at lines 274-289; no unit-1 or unit-2 implementation file is in the diff. Untracked scratch under .antigravity/ and .opencode/ is excluded as requested.

checks.evidence: The source has three blocking correctness gaps: validation occurs after bounded values are clipped (gpu_fuzzy_trader/run_pipeline.py:3210-3212, 3472-3474), the actual production catalog can shrink below 30 through dispersion filtering (gpu_fuzzy_trader/features/catalog.py:80-85), and feature-contract digests are recorded but not enforced for split, MTF, persistent Phase 2 archive, or RB reuse (gpu_fuzzy_trader/data/splitter.py:384-419; gpu_fuzzy_trader/run_pipeline.py:4407-4441).

The deterministic package reports its listed tests passing, but the new tests cover candidate ordering, digest sensitivity, digest presence, and a direct _run_phase2 rejection. They do not cover a constant/mostly-NaN required feature, validation data outside [-1,1] before/after scaling, split-cache invalidation, MTF/LWC archive invalidation, RB output invalidation, or a caller overriding the ledger digest.

Config/catalog/scaling changes reach the normal catalog/prune/Phase 2 path at gpu_fuzzy_trader/run_pipeline.py:1388-1405 and the OOS dataset preparation at gpu_fuzzy_trader/phases/phase5_oos.py:995-1011. The graph also shows split, MTF archive, Phase 2 archive, and strategy-loader callers, but those contracts do not consume or compare the new digest. The package's direct_dependents=[] summary is therefore incomplete for this review.

The feature-contract API presents a digest as lineage protection, but its enforcement is fragmented: records and the Phase 2 sidecar use it while split/archive/RB readers ignore it. The public ExperimentLedger.append implementation also allows record data to overwrite the computed digest because **dict(record) follows it at research_integrity.py:181-185.

The tracked diff contains only the 15 package files named in the task. Unit-1 and unit-2 production modules are unchanged. Untracked .antigravity/ and .opencode/ scratch was not used as a production-scope finding.

The supplied deterministic review package reports verification PASSED with zero failures, and the independent git diff --check inspection was clean. Passing verification does not cover the missing adversarial paths above.

findings.title: Bounded on-chain values are clipped before the Phase 2 rejection check
findings.description: The normal loader applies the inferred bounded_continuous scaling to validation frames before _run_phase2 calls validate_onchain_feature_ranges. The generic apply function clips every feature, so a validation value such as 2.5 becomes 1.0 and passes. An all-infinite training column is also treated as having no finite violations, then clipped. Validate raw supplied frames before scaling and make bounded_continuous pass-through reject rather than clip invalid values; add an integration test through _load_and_split_data.

findings.title: The actual supplied Phase 2 catalog is not guaranteed to contain all 30 features
findings.description: candidate_rule_feature_columns returns the 30-name contract, but build_rule_feature_specs immediately removes low-dispersion columns. A required feature with a constant or mostly warm-up-NaN training series is silently removed, so the production Phase 2 catalog has fewer than thirty supplied features. Bypass this filter for supplied_ff or otherwise fail closed when the final supplied catalog is not exactly the ordered 30; test the production build path with constant and NaN-heavy columns.

findings.title: Feature-contract digest is recorded but stale split, archive, and RB artifacts are still accepted
findings.description: The new digest is included in the Phase 2 sidecar identity and several manifests, but split cache loading never reads it. MTF composition loads existing archives without comparing the current digest, persistent Phase 2 archives validate only feature_signature, and standalone Phase 5 accepts stored RB outputs without a current digest check. Changing RULE_FEATURE_SOURCE_MODE or the on-chain manifest contract digest while keeping the same data and 30 columns can therefore reuse stale artifacts. Add the digest to each persisted identity and reject missing/mismatched values for splits, Phase 2/LWC/MTF archives, and RB strategy outputs.

findings.title: The digest omits registry fields that affect feature construction
findings.description: The transform payload includes output/source names, raw transform, scale family, delays, window, and min_periods, but omits source_cadence, target_cadence, aggregation, and allow_funding_gap from OnchainMetricSpec. A registry aggregation or cadence change without a simultaneous version/manifest update can leave feature_contract_digest unchanged. Serialize the complete registry/transform contract (and any authoritative scaling manifest) rather than selected fields.

findings.title: Ledger callers can overwrite the computed feature digest
findings.description: ExperimentLedger.append places feature_contract_digest before **dict(record) at lines 181-185. A caller that supplies the same key can write a stale or fabricated digest, defeating the ledger lineage field. Merge the record first and assign the computed digest last, or reject the reserved key.
